1.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_ref-1)**Certain award groups do not simply award one winner. They acknowledge several different recipients, have runners-up, and have third place. Since this is a specific recognition and is different from losing an award, runner-up mentions are considered wins in this award tally. For simplification and to avoid errors, each award in this list has been presumed to have had a prior nomination.

**[Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood")** is an American film actor, [director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer"), and [composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composer "Composer"). He also has contributed music to his films, either through performing, writing, or composing. He has appeared mainly in [western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)"), [action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film"), [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), and [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") films.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-Genres-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-TwoSides-3) Over his career, he has received several accolades including four [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), four [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), and two [Directors Guild of America Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Awards "Directors Guild of America Awards") as well as nominations for two [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards"), a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), and [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award"). He has been honored numerous prizes such as the [AFI Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI_Life_Achievement_Award "AFI Life Achievement Award") in 1996, the [Honorary César](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_C%C3%A9sar "Honorary César") in 1998, an [Honorary Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Golden_Lion "Honorary Golden Lion") in 2000, the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2000, the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") in 2003, the Stanley Kubrick [Britannia Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Award "Britannia Award") in 2006, the [Honorary Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Palme_d%27Or "Honorary Palme d'Or") in 2008, and the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 2009.

After beginning his acting career primarily with small uncredited film roles and television appearances, his career has spanned more than 60 years in both television and film productions. Eastwood appeared in several television series, most notably appearing on _[Rawhide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawhide\_(TV\_series) "Rawhide (TV series)")_. His role in the eight-season series led to his leading roles in the [spaghetti western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_western "Spaghetti western") trilogy _[A Fistful of Dollars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Fistful\_of\_Dollars "A Fistful of Dollars")_ (1964), _[For a Few Dollars More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_a\_Few\_Dollars\_More "For a Few Dollars More")_ (1965) and _[The Good, the Bad and the Ugly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good,\_the\_Bad\_and\_the\_Ugly "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly")_ (1966), which weren't released in the United States until 1967/68.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-RawFilms-4) Eastwood has played leading roles in 48 films, including the revisionist western _[Hang 'Em High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hang\_%27Em\_High "Hang 'Em High")_ (1968), the prison drama _[Escape from Alcatraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape\_from\_Alcatraz\_(film) "Escape from Alcatraz (film)")_ (1979), the romance drama _[The Bridges of Madison County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bridges\_of\_Madison\_County\_(film) "The Bridges of Madison County (film)")_ (1995), and the drama _[Gran Torino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Torino\_(film) "Gran Torino (film)")_ (2008). Eastwood's started directing in 1971, and in 1982, his debut as a producer began with two films, the action thriller _[Firefox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefox\_(film) "Firefox (film)")_ (1982) and the musical western _[Honkytonk Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honkytonk\_Man "Honkytonk Man")_ (1982).

Eastwood directed the biographical musical drama _[Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird\_(1988\_film) "Bird (1988 film)")_ (1988) for which he was first nominated for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"). He gained acclaim for directing the [revisionist Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revisionist_Western "Revisionist Western")_[Unforgiven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unforgiven "Unforgiven")_ (1992) for which he received the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") and the [Academy Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") as well as the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"). For the [neo-noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-noir "Neo-noir") mystery thriller _[Mystic River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystic\_River\_(film) "Mystic River (film)")_ (2003), he earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations for Picture and Director and a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nomination for Director. For the [sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama")_[Million Dollar Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million\_Dollar\_Baby "Million Dollar Baby")_ (2004) he won [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") for Best Picture and Best Director with a nomination for his first [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor"). The film also earned him a win for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director") as well as nomination for the [Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Score_Soundtrack_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media").

He directed the American [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") drama _[Flags of Our Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flags\_of\_Our\_Fathers\_(film) "Flags of Our Fathers (film)")_ (2005), and the Japanese [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") drama _[Letters from Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letters\_from\_Iwo\_Jima "Letters from Iwo Jima")_ (2006), the later of which earned him Academy Award nominations for Best Picture and Best Director. He directed the mystery crime drama _[Changeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changeling\_(film) "Changeling (film)")_ (2008) for which he was nominated for the [BAFTA Award for Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction"). He earned critical attention for directing and playing a grumpy widow and [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") veteran in the drama _[Gran Torino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Torino "Gran Torino")_ (2008) for which he also served as the film's composer earning a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song"). He directed the [docudrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docudrama "Docudrama")[sports film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama")_[Invictus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invictus\_(film) "Invictus (film)")_ (2009) earning a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director").

After an 8-year absence from the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") he returned with the biographical war drama _[American Sniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Sniper\_(film) "American Sniper (film)")_ (2014) for which he was nominated as a producer for the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). For the film he also received the [National Board of Review Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Director "National Board of Review Award for Best Director") as well as a nomination for the [Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directing – Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Outstanding_Directing_%E2%80%93_Feature_Film "Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directing – Feature Film").

On August 21, 1984, Eastwood was honored at a ceremony at [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman%27s_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") to record his hand and footprints in cement. In May 1994, Eastwood was presented with France's medal of Comandeur de L' Ordre des Arts et des Lettres at the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival"). [Jeanne Moreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Moreau "Jeanne Moreau") commented, "Its remarkable that a man so important in European cinema has found the time to come here and spend twelve days watching movies with us".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-mcgilligan-5): 491  The jury included two people Eastwood knew well: [Catherine Deneuve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Deneuve "Catherine Deneuve"), with whom he had an affair back in the mid-1960s, and [Lalo Schifrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalo_Schifrin "Lalo Schifrin"), who had composed most of the jazz tracks to his _Dirty Harry_ films.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-mcgilligan-5): 491  Eastwood received the AFI Life Achievement Award in 1996 and received an honorary degree from AFI in 2009. Eastwood is one of only two people to have been twice nominated for Best Actor and Best Director for the same film (_Unforgiven_ and _Million Dollar Baby_) the other being [Warren Beatty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Beatty "Warren Beatty") (_Heaven Can Wait_ and _Reds_). Along with Beatty, [Robert Redford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Redford "Robert Redford"), [Richard Attenborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough"), [Kevin Costner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Costner "Kevin Costner"), and [Mel Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Gibson "Mel Gibson"), he is one of the few directors best known as an actor to win an Academy Award for directing. On February 27, 2005, at age 74, he became one of only three living directors (along with [Miloš Forman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milo%C5%A1_Forman "Miloš Forman") and [Francis Ford Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ford_Coppola "Francis Ford Coppola")) to have directed two Best Picture winners. He is also, at age 74, the oldest recipient of the Academy Award for Best Director. Eastwood has also directed five actors in Academy Award–winning performances: [Gene Hackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Hackman "Gene Hackman") in _Unforgiven_, [Tim Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Robbins "Tim Robbins") and [Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn "Sean Penn") in _Mystic River_, and [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman") and [Hilary Swank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Swank "Hilary Swank") in _Million Dollar Baby_.

> I will never win an Oscar and do you know why? First of all, because I'm not Jewish. Secondly, because I make too much money for those old farts in the Academy. Thirdly, and most importantly, because I don't give a fuck.

— Clint Eastwood during the 1970s, _14 Things You Never Knew About Clint Eastwood's 'Unforgiven'_[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-7): 260

Eastwood has received numerous other awards, including a [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2000. He received an honorary degree from [University of the Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Pacific_(United_States) "University of the Pacific (United States)") in 2006, and an honorary degree from [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California") in 2007. In 1995 he received the honorary Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award for lifetime achievement in film producing.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-8) In 2006, he received a nomination for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") in the category of Best Score Soundtrack Album For Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media for _Million Dollar Baby_. In 2007, Eastwood was the first recipient of the Jack Valenti Humanitarian Award, an annual award presented by the [MPAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPAA "MPAA") to individuals in the motion picture industry whose work has reached out positively and respectfully to the world. He received the award for his work on the 2006 films _Flags of Our Fathers_ and _Letters from Iwo Jima_.

On December 6, 2006, California Governor [Arnold Schwarzenegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Schwarzenegger "Arnold Schwarzenegger") and First Lady [Maria Shriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Shriver "Maria Shriver") inducted Eastwood into the [California Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Hall_of_Fame "California Hall of Fame") located at [The California Museum for History, Women, and the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_California_Museum_for_History,_Women,_and_the_Arts "The California Museum for History, Women, and the Arts"). In early 2007, Eastwood was presented with the highest civilian distinction in France, [Légion d'honneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9gion_d%27honneur "Légion d'honneur"), at a ceremony in Paris. French President [Jacques Chirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Chirac "Jacques Chirac") told Eastwood that he embodied "the best of Hollywood".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-9) On November 13, 2009, Clint Eastwood was made French [Legion of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Honor "Legion of Honor") Commander, which represents the third highest of five classes associated with this award.

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Eastwood_received_an_honorary_Doctor_of_Humane_Letters_from_the_University_of_Southern_California.jpg/250px-Eastwood_received_an_honorary_Doctor_of_Humane_Letters_from_the_University_of_Southern_California.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eastwood_received_an_honorary_Doctor_of_Humane_Letters_from_the_University_of_Southern_California.jpg)

Eastwood receiving an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from the University of Southern California in 2007

On May 27, 2007, Eastwood received an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from the University of Southern California. On September 22, 2007, Eastwood was awarded an honorary [Doctor of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Music "Doctor of Music") degree from the [Berklee College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berklee_College_of_Music "Berklee College of Music") at the [Monterey Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_Jazz_Festival "Monterey Jazz Festival"), on which he serves as an active board member. Upon receiving the award he gave a speech, claiming, "It's one of the great honors I'll cherish in this lifetime."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-10) Eastwood received the 2008 Best Actor award from the [National Board of Review of Motion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_of_Motion_Pictures "National Board of Review of Motion Pictures") for his performance in _Gran Torino_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-NBR_award-11) On April 29, 2009, the Japanese government announced that Eastwood was to receive the [Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Rising_Sun "Order of the Rising Sun"), which represents the third highest of eight classes associated with this award.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-12)

In October 2009, he was honored by the Lumière Award (in honor of the [Lumière Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auguste_and_Louis_Lumi%C3%A8re "Auguste and Louis Lumière"), inventors of the [Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography")) during the first edition of the [Lumière Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumi%C3%A8re_Film_Festival "Lumière Film Festival") in [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyon "Lyon"), France. This award honors his entire career and his major contribution to the 7th Art. In February 2010, Eastwood was recognized by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") with an arts and humanities award. Obama called Eastwood's films "essays in individuality, hard truths and the essence of what it means to be American."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-13)

Eastwood does not have a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-FOOTNOTELevy2025271-14)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") awards and nominations[![Image 1: Clint Eastwood at the 1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Clint_Eastwood_Cannes_1993.jpg/250px-Clint_Eastwood_Cannes_1993.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clint_Eastwood_Cannes_1993.jpg)

Note

1.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_ref-1)**Certain award groups do not simply award one winner. They acknowledge several different recipients, have runners-up, and have third place. Since this is a specific recognition and is different from losing an award, runner-up mentions are considered wins in this award tally. For simplification and to avoid errors, each award in this list has been presumed to have had a prior nomination.

**[Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood")** is an American film actor, [director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer"), and [composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composer "Composer"). He also has contributed music to his films, either through performing, writing, or composing. He has appeared mainly in [western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)"), [action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film"), [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), and [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") films.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-Genres-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-TwoSides-3) Over his career, he has received several accolades including four [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), four [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), and two [Directors Guild of America Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Awards "Directors Guild of America Awards") as well as nominations for two [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards"), a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), and [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award"). He has been honored numerous prizes such as the [AFI Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI_Life_Achievement_Award "AFI Life Achievement Award") in 1996, the [Honorary César](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_C%C3%A9sar "Honorary César") in 1998, an [Honorary Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Golden_Lion "Honorary Golden Lion") in 2000, the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2000, the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") in 2003, the Stanley Kubrick [Britannia Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Award "Britannia Award") in 2006, the [Honorary Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Palme_d%27Or "Honorary Palme d'Or") in 2008, and the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 2009.

After beginning his acting career primarily with small uncredited film roles and television appearances, his career has spanned more than 60 years in both television and film productions. Eastwood appeared in several television series, most notably appearing on _[Rawhide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawhide\_(TV\_series) "Rawhide (TV series)")_. His role in the eight-season series led to his leading roles in the [spaghetti western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_western "Spaghetti western") trilogy _[A Fistful of Dollars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Fistful\_of\_Dollars "A Fistful of Dollars")_ (1964), _[For a Few Dollars More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_a\_Few\_Dollars\_More "For a Few Dollars More")_ (1965) and _[The Good, the Bad and the Ugly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good,\_the\_Bad\_and\_the\_Ugly "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly")_ (1966), which weren't released in the United States until 1967/68.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-RawFilms-4) Eastwood has played leading roles in 48 films, including the revisionist western _[Hang 'Em High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hang\_%27Em\_High "Hang 'Em High")_ (1968), the prison drama _[Escape from Alcatraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape\_from\_Alcatraz\_(film) "Escape from Alcatraz (film)")_ (1979), the romance drama _[The Bridges of Madison County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bridges\_of\_Madison\_County\_(film) "The Bridges of Madison County (film)")_ (1995), and the drama _[Gran Torino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Torino\_(film) "Gran Torino (film)")_ (2008). Eastwood's started directing in 1971, and in 1982, his debut as a producer began with two films, the action thriller _[Firefox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefox\_(film) "Firefox (film)")_ (1982) and the musical western _[Honkytonk Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honkytonk\_Man "Honkytonk Man")_ (1982).

Eastwood directed the biographical musical drama _[Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird\_(1988\_film) "Bird (1988 film)")_ (1988) for which he was first nominated for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"). He gained acclaim for directing the [revisionist Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revisionist_Western "Revisionist Western")_[Unforgiven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unforgiven "Unforgiven")_ (1992) for which he received the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") and the [Academy Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") as well as the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"). For the [neo-noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-noir "Neo-noir") mystery thriller _[Mystic River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystic\_River\_(film) "Mystic River (film)")_ (2003), he earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations for Picture and Director and a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nomination for Director. For the [sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama")_[Million Dollar Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million\_Dollar\_Baby "Million Dollar Baby")_ (2004) he won [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") for Best Picture and Best Director with a nomination for his first [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor"). The film also earned him a win for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director") as well as nomination for the [Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Score_Soundtrack_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media").

He directed the American [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") drama _[Flags of Our Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flags\_of\_Our\_Fathers\_(film) "Flags of Our Fathers (film)")_ (2005), and the Japanese [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") drama _[Letters from Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letters\_from\_Iwo\_Jima "Letters from Iwo Jima")_ (2006), the later of which earned him Academy Award nominations for Best Picture and Best Director. He directed the mystery crime drama _[Changeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changeling\_(film) "Changeling (film)")_ (2008) for which he was nominated for the [BAFTA Award for Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction"). He earned critical attention for directing and playing a grumpy widow and [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") veteran in the drama _[Gran Torino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Torino "Gran Torino")_ (2008) for which he also served as the film's composer earning a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song"). He directed the [docudrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docudrama "Docudrama")[sports film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama")_[Invictus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invictus\_(film) "Invictus (film)")_ (2009) earning a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director").

After an 8-year absence from the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") he returned with the biographical war drama _[American Sniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Sniper\_(film) "American Sniper (film)")_ (2014) for which he was nominated as a producer for the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). For the film he also received the [National Board of Review Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Director "National Board of Review Award for Best Director") as well as a nomination for the [Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directing – Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Outstanding_Directing_%E2%80%93_Feature_Film "Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directing – Feature Film").

On August 21, 1984, Eastwood was honored at a ceremony at [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman%27s_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") to record his hand and footprints in cement. In May 1994, Eastwood was presented with France's medal of Comandeur de L' Ordre des Arts et des Lettres at the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival"). [Jeanne Moreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Moreau "Jeanne Moreau") commented, "Its remarkable that a man so important in European cinema has found the time to come here and spend twelve days watching movies with us".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-mcgilligan-5): 491  The jury included two people Eastwood knew well: [Catherine Deneuve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Deneuve "Catherine Deneuve"), with whom he had an affair back in the mid-1960s, and [Lalo Schifrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalo_Schifrin "Lalo Schifrin"), who had composed most of the jazz tracks to his _Dirty Harry_ films.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-mcgilligan-5): 491  Eastwood received the AFI Life Achievement Award in 1996 and received an honorary degree from AFI in 2009. Eastwood is one of only two people to have been twice nominated for Best Actor and Best Director for the same film (_Unforgiven_ and _Million Dollar Baby_) the other being [Warren Beatty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Beatty "Warren Beatty") (_Heaven Can Wait_ and _Reds_). Along with Beatty, [Robert Redford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Redford "Robert Redford"), [Richard Attenborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough"), [Kevin Costner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Costner "Kevin Costner"), and [Mel Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Gibson "Mel Gibson"), he is one of the few directors best known as an actor to win an Academy Award for directing. On February 27, 2005, at age 74, he became one of only three living directors (along with [Miloš Forman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milo%C5%A1_Forman "Miloš Forman") and [Francis Ford Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ford_Coppola "Francis Ford Coppola")) to have directed two Best Picture winners. He is also, at age 74, the oldest recipient of the Academy Award for Best Director. Eastwood has also directed five actors in Academy Award–winning performances: [Gene Hackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Hackman "Gene Hackman") in _Unforgiven_, [Tim Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Robbins "Tim Robbins") and [Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn "Sean Penn") in _Mystic River_, and [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman") and [Hilary Swank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Swank "Hilary Swank") in _Million Dollar Baby_.

> I will never win an Oscar and do you know why? First of all, because I'm not Jewish. Secondly, because I make too much money for those old farts in the Academy. Thirdly, and most importantly, because I don't give a fuck.

— Clint Eastwood during the 1970s, _14 Things You Never Knew About Clint Eastwood's 'Unforgiven'_[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-7): 260

Eastwood has received numerous other awards, including a [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2000. He received an honorary degree from [University of the Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Pacific_(United_States) "University of the Pacific (United States)") in 2006, and an honorary degree from [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California") in 2007. In 1995 he received the honorary Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award for lifetime achievement in film producing.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-8) In 2006, he received a nomination for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") in the category of Best Score Soundtrack Album For Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media for _Million Dollar Baby_. In 2007, Eastwood was the first recipient of the Jack Valenti Humanitarian Award, an annual award presented by the [MPAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPAA "MPAA") to individuals in the motion picture industry whose work has reached out positively and respectfully to the world. He received the award for his work on the 2006 films _Flags of Our Fathers_ and _Letters from Iwo Jima_.

On December 6, 2006, California Governor [Arnold Schwarzenegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Schwarzenegger "Arnold Schwarzenegger") and First Lady [Maria Shriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Shriver "Maria Shriver") inducted Eastwood into the [California Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Hall_of_Fame "California Hall of Fame") located at [The California Museum for History, Women, and the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_California_Museum_for_History,_Women,_and_the_Arts "The California Museum for History, Women, and the Arts"). In early 2007, Eastwood was presented with the highest civilian distinction in France, [Légion d'honneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9gion_d%27honneur "Légion d'honneur"), at a ceremony in Paris. French President [Jacques Chirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Chirac "Jacques Chirac") told Eastwood that he embodied "the best of Hollywood".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-9) On November 13, 2009, Clint Eastwood was made French [Legion of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Honor "Legion of Honor") Commander, which represents the third highest of five classes associated with this award.

Eastwood receiving an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from the University of Southern California in 2007

On May 27, 2007, Eastwood received an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from the University of Southern California. On September 22, 2007, Eastwood was awarded an honorary [Doctor of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Music "Doctor of Music") degree from the [Berklee College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berklee_College_of_Music "Berklee College of Music") at the [Monterey Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_Jazz_Festival "Monterey Jazz Festival"), on which he serves as an active board member. Upon receiving the award he gave a speech, claiming, "It's one of the great honors I'll cherish in this lifetime."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-10) Eastwood received the 2008 Best Actor award from the [National Board of Review of Motion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_of_Motion_Pictures "National Board of Review of Motion Pictures") for his performance in _Gran Torino_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-NBR_award-11) On April 29, 2009, the Japanese government announced that Eastwood was to receive the [Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Neck Ribbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Rising_Sun "Order of the Rising Sun"), which represents the third highest of eight classes associated with this award.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-12)

In October 2009, he was honored by the Lumière Award (in honor of the [Lumière Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auguste_and_Louis_Lumi%C3%A8re "Auguste and Louis Lumière"), inventors of the [Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography")) during the first edition of the [Lumière Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumi%C3%A8re_Film_Festival "Lumière Film Festival") in [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyon "Lyon"), France. This award honors his entire career and his major contribution to the 7th Art. In February 2010, Eastwood was recognized by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") with an arts and humanities award. Obama called Eastwood's films "essays in individuality, hard truths and the essence of what it means to be American."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Clint_Eastwood#cite_note-13)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of those who have served as [President of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru "President of Peru") ([head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru")) from its establishment to the present. The office was established by the [1822 Constituent Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru_(1822) "Constituent Congress of Peru (1822)"), after the resignation of [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") to his position as Protector of Peru and his subsequent departure from the country.

The first president was [José de la Riva Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_la_Riva_Ag%C3%BCero "José de la Riva Agüero") and the current officeholder is [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar "José María Balcázar"). In the history of the position, there has been several political crises, [caudillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudillo "Caudillo"), barracks revolt, civil wars, death of the incumbent, coups d'état, parliamentary attempts to remove the presidency,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-1) one [self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup "1992 Peruvian self-coup"), and vacancies dictated by the congress. The list is based on the official list of rulers by the Peruvian Congress, as well as the constitutions, laws, and decrees in each case.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-3)

Even though they were not presidents, the list includes the [Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertadores "Libertadores") San Martín and [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar") due to their historical relevance in the independence of Peru and its consolidation. The country's name was changed from "Peruvian Republic" (_República peruana_) to "Republic of Peru" (_República del Perú_) in 1980, after the [1979 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Peru_(1979) "Constitution of Peru (1979)") came into effect.

**Political parties:**

**Far-right:**

*   [Fujimorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujimorism "Fujimorism")(_Cambio 90_/ _Let's Go Neighbor_)
*   [Revolutionary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Union_(Peru) "Revolutionary Union (Peru)")(_Unión Revolucionaria_, UR)
*   [Odriist National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odriist_National_Union "Odriist National Union")(_Unión Nacional Odriista_, UNO)

**Right wing:**

*   [Civilista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilista_Party "Civilista Party") (_Partido Civil_, PC)
*   [Constitutional Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Party_(Peru) "Constitutional Party (Peru)")(_Partido Constitucional_)
*   [Reformist Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformist_Democratic_Party "Reformist Democratic Party")(_Partido Democrático Reformista_)
*   [Peruvian Democratic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Democratic_Movement "Peruvian Democratic Movement")(_Movimiento Democrático Peruano_, MDP)
*   [National Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Front_(Peru) "National Democratic Front (Peru)")(_Frente Democrático Nacional_)

**Centre-right:**

*   [Peruvian Aprista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Aprista_Party "Peruvian Aprista Party")(_Partido Aprista Peruano_, APRA)
*   [Peruvians for Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvians_for_Change "Peruvians for Change")(_Peruanos Por el Kambio_, PPK)
*   [Popular Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Action_(Peru) "Popular Action (Peru)")(_Acción Popular_, AP)
*   [We Are Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Peru "We Are Peru")(_Partido Democrático Somos Perú, PDSP_)

**Centrist:**

*   [Possible Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Possible_Peru "Possible Peru")(_Perú Posible_, PP)
*   [Purple Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Party "Purple Party")(_Partido Morado_, PM)

**Centre-left:**

*   [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(Peru) "Democratic Party (Peru)")(_Partido Demócrata_, PD)
*   [Peruvian Nationalist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Nationalist_Party "Peruvian Nationalist Party")(_Partido Nacionalista Peruano_, PNP)

**Far-left:**

*   [Free Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Peru "Free Peru")(_Perú Libre_, PL)

**Others:**

*   [Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician")
*   [Military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Armed_Forces "Peruvian Armed Forces")

1.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-3 "Jump up")**The official website of Congress includes a list of "presidents and rulers of the Republic" from 1821 until 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2) It lists a total of 130 governments from [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") until [Pedro Castillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Castillo "Pedro Castillo"), but does not separate constitutional presidencies from dictatorships nor interim governments. This Wikipedia list includes a total of 40 presidents and 53 presidencies from 1821 until 2021.
2.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-6 "Jump up")**Some authors regard [Francisco Xavier de Luna Pizarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Xavier_de_Luna_Pizarro "Francisco Xavier de Luna Pizarro"), president of Congress, as _de facto_ interim ruler for a signle day, between San Martin's resignation and the appointment of the Supreme Junta.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2) By this logic, [Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toribio_Rodr%C3%ADguez_de_Mendoza "Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza") should also be considered interim president, as he was chosen as temporary head of Congress during the election of their official members.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-5)

Andrés de Santa Cruz had been the _de facto_ governor of Peru in the name of Bolivar.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_1,_p._180-21)

9.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-33 "Jump up")**Recognized in the Southern provinces; captured Orbegoso and briefly took over Lima in January 1834, but was expelled by the citizens. Continued to claim power until being betrayed by his own men, who reconciled with Orbegoso on 24 April.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_2,_pp._69%E2%80%9375-32)
10.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-36 "Jump up")**Controlled Lima until 30 December 1835, when Orbegoso's troops entered the city, although infighting continued until 6 January 1836. Was defeated in the [Battle of Socabaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Battle_of_Socabaya&action=edit&redlink=1 "Battle of Socabaya (page does not exist)") on 7 February and executed a few days later, on 18 February.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_2,_pp._92%E2%80%93111-35)
11.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-40 "Jump up")**Orbegoso resigned the Peruvian presidency on 3 August 1836, after promoting the creation of the [Peru–Bolivian Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru%E2%80%93Bolivian_Confederation "Peru–Bolivian Confederation") of [Andrés de Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Santa_Cruz "Andrés de Santa Cruz").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-norp-38) He had already been given the "supreme power" on 8 July 1835, dring the war against Salaverry.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-39)
12.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-43 "Jump up")**Already proclaimed Supreme Protector of [South Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Peru "South Peru") (17 March) and [North Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Peru "North Peru") (6 August).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-41)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-norp-38) Ratified by the [Congress of Tacna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Tacna "Congress of Tacna") on 1 May 1837.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-42)
13.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-45 "Jump up")**Orbegoso declared himself independent on 30 July 1838, but was defeated three weeks later by Gamarra's restoration forces at the [Battle of Portada de Guías](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Portada_de_Gu%C3%ADas "Battle of Portada de Guías"), near Lima. Santa Cruz appointed Riva Agüero as his replacement, at [Tarma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarma "Tarma").

45.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-141 "Jump up")**The [1919 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1919_Peruvian_presidential_election "1919 Peruvian presidential election"), held on May 18, resulted in a clear victory for Leguía, but the Supreme Tribunal denounced several irregularities by almost all parties.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-138) Leguía secured his victory through a coup two months later, on July 4.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-139) The election results, and Leguía's position, were ratified by Congress on October 12.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-140)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of those who have served as [President of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru "President of Peru") ([head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru")) from its establishment to the present. The office was established by the [1822 Constituent Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru_(1822) "Constituent Congress of Peru (1822)"), after the resignation of [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") to his position as Protector of Peru and his subsequent departure from the country.

The first president was [José de la Riva Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_la_Riva_Ag%C3%BCero "José de la Riva Agüero") and the current officeholder is [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar "José María Balcázar"). In the history of the position, there has been several political crises, [caudillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudillo "Caudillo"), barracks revolt, civil wars, death of the incumbent, coups d'état, parliamentary attempts to remove the presidency,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-1) one [self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup "1992 Peruvian self-coup"), and vacancies dictated by the congress. The list is based on the official list of rulers by the Peruvian Congress, as well as the constitutions, laws, and decrees in each case.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-3)

Even though they were not presidents, the list includes the [Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertadores "Libertadores") San Martín and [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar") due to their historical relevance in the independence of Peru and its consolidation. The country's name was changed from "Peruvian Republic" (_República peruana_) to "Republic of Peru" (_República del Perú_) in 1980, after the [1979 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Peru_(1979) "Constitution of Peru (1979)") came into effect.

**Political parties:**

**Far-right:**

*   [Fujimorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujimorism "Fujimorism")(_Cambio 90_/ _Let's Go Neighbor_)
*   [Revolutionary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Union_(Peru) "Revolutionary Union (Peru)")(_Unión Revolucionaria_, UR)
*   [Odriist National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odriist_National_Union "Odriist National Union")(_Unión Nacional Odriista_, UNO)

**Right wing:**

*   [Civilista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilista_Party "Civilista Party") (_Partido Civil_, PC)
*   [Constitutional Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Party_(Peru) "Constitutional Party (Peru)")(_Partido Constitucional_)
*   [Reformist Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformist_Democratic_Party "Reformist Democratic Party")(_Partido Democrático Reformista_)
*   [Peruvian Democratic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Democratic_Movement "Peruvian Democratic Movement")(_Movimiento Democrático Peruano_, MDP)
*   [National Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Front_(Peru) "National Democratic Front (Peru)")(_Frente Democrático Nacional_)

**Centre-right:**

*   [Peruvian Aprista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Aprista_Party "Peruvian Aprista Party")(_Partido Aprista Peruano_, APRA)
*   [Peruvians for Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvians_for_Change "Peruvians for Change")(_Peruanos Por el Kambio_, PPK)
*   [Popular Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Action_(Peru) "Popular Action (Peru)")(_Acción Popular_, AP)
*   [We Are Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Peru "We Are Peru")(_Partido Democrático Somos Perú, PDSP_)

**Centrist:**

*   [Possible Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Possible_Peru "Possible Peru")(_Perú Posible_, PP)
*   [Purple Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Party "Purple Party")(_Partido Morado_, PM)

**Centre-left:**

*   [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(Peru) "Democratic Party (Peru)")(_Partido Demócrata_, PD)
*   [Peruvian Nationalist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Nationalist_Party "Peruvian Nationalist Party")(_Partido Nacionalista Peruano_, PNP)

**Far-left:**

*   [Free Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Peru "Free Peru")(_Perú Libre_, PL)

**Others:**

*   [Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician")
*   [Military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Armed_Forces "Peruvian Armed Forces")

9.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-33 "Jump up")**Recognized in the Southern provinces; captured Orbegoso and briefly took over Lima in January 1834, but was expelled by the citizens. 13.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-45 "Jump up")**Orbegoso declared himself independent on 30 July 1838, but was defeated three weeks later by Gamarra's restoration forces at the [Battle of Portada de Guías](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Portada_de_Gu%C3%ADas "Battle of Portada de Guías"), near Lima. # Peru names eighth president in a decade after incumbent's ouster

19 February 2026

Share

Save

[Add as preferred on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=bbc.com)

Vanessa Buschschlüter and

Yang Tian

![Image 1: Getty Images Peru's new interim President José María Balcázar wearing a black blazer, red tie, and a sash of Peru's flag.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/3c1e/live/953f17b0-0d54-11f1-b5e2-dd58fc65f0f6.jpg.webp)Getty Images

José María Balcázar will only be in power for a few months until a new president is chosen in the general election

Peru has a new interim president following [the removal from office of José Jerí](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cz7gvdx457vo) by Congress over allegations of influence peddling, which Jerí has denied.

Member of Congress elected José María Balcázar, 83, to lead the country on an interim basis until the end of July - when a new president, who will be chosen in a general election, will be sworn in.

Balcázar, from the left-wing Free Peru party, is the eighth president to govern Peru since 2016, with several previous leaders also deposed by Congress.

He said he would "guarantee the people of Peru a peaceful and transparent democratic and electoral transition".

The first round of the presidential election will be held on 12 April, but with dozens of candidates vying for the top job it is unlikely that any of them will receive the 50% of the votes needed to win outright.

A run-off between the top two candidates, due to be held on 7 June, is therefore highly likely.

While previous presidents can run for a second term, the two terms cannot follow on from each other, meaning that both José Jerí and José María Balcázar are barred from standing.

Opinion polls suggest the top two candidates are right-wing Congresswoman Keiko Fujimori, whose father Alberto Fujimori ruled from 1990 to 2000, and the mayor of the capital, Lima, Rafael López Aliaga.

Advertisement

But the polls suggest that the vast majority of Peruvians have not yet decided who they will cast their vote for.

José María Balcázar will be in charge until the swearing-in ceremony of whoever wins is held on 28 July.

The former judge has been criticised for his opposition in Congress against a bill which outlawed child marriage. The bill was approved despite his vote against it.

Balcázar takes the reins of power at a time when trust in politicians is very low and has been further rocked by the graft allegations which led to Jerí's ouster.

One Lima resident told the Reuters news agency: "In 10 years, how many presidents have we had? It's an enormous setback for the country."

Another was quoted as saying that he had "gotten used to this crisis, because we're really in a crisis where Congress only dedicates itself to changing the president and looking out for their own well-being".

Jerí was forced out of office by Congress on Tuesday when lawmakers voted overwhelmingly in favour of censure motion, which led to his immediate removal from the presidency.

The vote followed a scandal dubbed "Chifa-gate" - a local name for Chinese-Peruvian fusion food and the restaurants which serve it.

The controversy centred on several meetings Jerí had outside his official schedule with a Chinese businessman.

This businessman, Zhihua Yang, was under government scrutiny and while Jerí apologised for the meetings, the fact that he had not disclosed them - as he is obliged to do under Peruvia law - arose suspicion.

In one of the videos, Jerí could be seen wearing a hooded top during a late-night visit at one of Yang's restaurants.

He denied any wrongdoing and accused his rivals of a public smear campaign but he soon faced further criticism after it emerged that state contracts had been awarded to a number of women following late-night meetings they had with him in the presidential palace.

Jerí maintains his innocence and following his ouster said that it had been an honour to have served as Peru's president.

He was in office for just four months, having replaced former leader Dina Boluarte, who was impeached in October last year.

verifications.claim_text: Peru has had eight presidents take office in the past ten years.
verifications.original_text:
Title: Peru Is About to Elect Its Ninth President in a Decade. What Happened to the Other Eight? URL Source: https://www.cfr.org/articles/peru-is-about-to-elect-its-ninth-president-in-a-decade-what-happened-to-the-other-eight Published Time: 2026-04-09T11:31:14-04:00 Markdown Content: Peru has earned a reputation for its so-called presidential curse, having had eight presidents take office in the past ten years. Many resigned or were impeached, and some are serving time at Barbadillo Prison in the capital, Lima, known as Peru’s “[presidential prison](https://www.npr.org/2023/07/08/1186632810/perus-special-jail-for-ex-leaders-is-all-full-up).” José Jerí became the most recent president to be removed from office on February 17—just four months into his term—over corruption allegations. Peru’s rapid leadership turnover has been driven largely by invoking a constitutional clause allowing Congress to impeach and remove leaders with a two-thirds majority for reasons of “permanent moral or physical incapacity.” This, combined with political clashes between the executive and legislative branches, frequent scandals, and a lack of legislative majorities, has fueled chronic political instability. The current cycle of revolving leadership traces back to the presidency of Pedro Pablo Kuczynski, who took office in 2016. With a presidential runoff scheduled for June 7, Peru will soon inaugurate its ninth leader in roughly as many years. Here’s a look at who has led the South American country over the past decade, and why they left office. #### Pedro Pablo Kuczynski _July 2016–March 2018_ Kuczynski, widely known as PPK, had previously served as both prime minister and minister of economy and finance under President Alejandro Toledo. Peru’s Congress [initiated](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/dec/15/impeachment-proceedings-against-perus-president-pedro-pablo-kuczynski) impeachment proceedings against Kuczynski in late 2017, following allegations that he had lied about receiving payments related to the [Odebrecht scandal](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-41109132) that ran from 2001 to 2016. As part of this regionwide corruption scheme, Brazilian construction conglomerate Odebrecht paid [nearly $800 million](https://www.icij.org/investigations/bribery-division/leak-exposes-millions-of-dollars-in-new-payments-in-odebrecht-cash-for-contracts-scandal/) in bribes to officials across twelve countries—most of which were in Latin America—to secure major public contracts. Though Kuczynski [survived](https://www.wsj.com/articles/perus-president-survives-impeachment-vote-1513917791?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqex4xDZ2Qy_TB5iiJKH8cW35dG3Me2T4R9BFilYWkkyRDB6YW5yAUfGyT2JSds%3D&gaa_ts=69caa25e&gaa_sig=9ecA8WRNni_4lFVl6S3sChqmPsKfEAq4DXL5w9nHPw7xcgpLmIVU6ajBa-ghIW-JIg-kyqdwuvEzdBqS7aCMjA%3D%3D) an initial impeachment vote, he [resigned](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-43492421) in March 2018 in the face of a second impeachment effort. In April 2019, Kuczynski was arrested for alleged money laundering in the Odebrecht case and placed under house arrest. He was granted conditional release in 2022. As of 2023, prosecutors [are seeking](https://english.elpais.com/international/2023-05-13/prosecutors-seek-35-year-jail-term-for-former-peruvian-president-over-odebrecht-scandal.html) a thirty-five-year prison sentence; Kuczynski is still on trial. In June 2025, he was given an eighteen-month travel ban after getting caught attempting to [leave](https://www.riotimesonline.com/former-president-kuczynski-grounded-in-peru-over-bribery-allegations/) the country. #### Martín Vizcarra _March 2018–November 2020_ Vizcarra faced impeachment proceedings in September 2020 for allegedly misusing public funds, though opposition leaders [failed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/9/19/perus-president-martin-vizcarra-survives-impeachment-vote) to amass enough support for the effort. The next month, several political factions [filed](https://web.archive.org/web/20230410183631/https://laley.pe/art/10207/otra-mocion-de-censura-contra-vizcarra-nuevamente-la-vacancia-presidencial) fresh impeachment articles, citing the president’s presumed “permanent moral incapacity.” They [alleged](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/peru-lawmakers-vote-to-remove-president-over-allegedly-taking-bribes) Vizcarra had accepted more than $600,000 in bribes during his tenure as governor of the southern Moquegua region from 2011 to 2014. Vizcarra was officially removed from office that November following a [105–19 vote](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-54872826). ![Image 1:

A demonstrator holds a poster with a picture of interim President Manuel Merino as they protest against Congress’s decision to remove former President Martín Vizcarra in Lima, Peru, on November 14, 2020.

](https://assets.cfr.org/images/t_cfr_3_2/f_auto/w_1920/v1775589043/PeruProtest_A/PeruProtest_A.jpg) A demonstrator holds a poster with a picture of interim President Manuel Merino as they protest against Congress’s decision to remove former President Martín Vizcarra in Lima, Peru, on November 14, 2020. Sebastian Castañeda/Reuters In November 2025, Vizcarra was [sentenced](https://www.occrp.org/en/news/peru-jails-ex-president-vizcarra-after-14-years-corruption-sentence) to fourteen years in prison at Barbadillo after being convicted of corruption. He was also ordered to pay almost seven hundred thousand dollars in compensation—jointly with other defendants—and barred from public office for nine years. #### Manuel Merino _November 2020_ Merino served only for five days before [resigning](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-54953546) on November 15 amid widespread protests that accused Congress of staging a parliamentary coup after the ouster of the popular Vizcarra. The demonstrations reached a critical point when police [killed](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/15/two-killed-as-huge-pro-democracy-protests-continue-in-peru) two protesters, sparking widespread outrage and prompting Merino to step down. Merino had previously served as president of Congress, [presiding over](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/10/peru-coup-accusations-head-of-congress-made-president-predecessor-ousted) Vizcarra’s impeachment proceedings. Half of his cabinet also resigned. His presidency is the shortest in modern Peruvian history. #### Francisco Sagasti _November 2020–July 2021_ Sagasti [served](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/16/world/americas/Peru-president-Francisco-Sagasti.html) as interim president for less than a year following Merino’s resignation. A centrist leader in Congress, Sagasti was sworn into office on November 17, 2020, marking Peru’s third president in a single week. He remained in office until the winner of the general election was inaugurated in July 2021. Sagasti’s Purple Party had been the only one in Congress to vote against Vizcarra’s impeachment in November 2020. Many Peruvians [hoped](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/perus-congress-selects-lawmaker-from-centrist-party-as-new-leader) his leadership could calm the country following Merino’s abrupt resignation. #### Pedro Castillo _July 2021–December 2022_ After taking office, Castillo faced significant congressional opposition over what policymakers considered to be radical proposals, including calls to nationalize major industries, such as mining and gas, and rewrite the constitution. He also faced accusations of corruption, including for his [alleged involvement](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/12/26/peru-arrests-three-police-generals-amid-castillo-corruption-probe) in a “pay-for-promotion” scheme involving police and military officers and for [unfairly favoring](https://www.occrp.org/en/news/perus-congress-accepts-corruption-charges-against-president-pedro-castillo) bids by the Puente Tarata construction consortium when awarding public works contracts. Castillo survived two impeachment attempts between November 2021 and March 2022. Facing a third impeachment, Castillo [launched](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/dec/07/peru-president-detained-pedro-castillo-coup) an _autogolpe_, or self-coup, in December 2022, announcing his plans to dissolve Congress and install an emergency government to rule by decree. He also called for new legislative elections. Hours after his proclamation, lawmakers [convened](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2022/12/07/peru-s-castillo-dissolves-congress-ahead-of-3rd-removal-try_6006915_4.html) anyway and overwhelmingly voted to impeach him. Soon after, Castillo was arrested on charges of conspiracy and rebellion after attempting to seek asylum at the Mexican Embassy in Lima. In November 2025, a court [sentenced](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/27/former-peru-president-pedro-castillo-sentenced-to-11-5-years-in-prison) Castillo to 11.5 years in prison. ![Image 2:

Interim President Dina Boluarte waves after being sworn in following the removal of President Pedro Castillo in an impeachment trial, in Lima, Peru, on December 7, 2022.

](https://assets.cfr.org/images/t_cfr_3_2/f_auto/w_1920/v1775589049/PeruElectionBoluarte_A/PeruElectionBoluarte_A.jpg) Interim President Dina Boluarte waves after being sworn in following the removal of President Pedro Castillo in an impeachment trial, in Lima, Peru, on December 7, 2022. Sebastian Castañeda/Reuters #### Dina Boluarte _December 2022–October 2025_ Boluarte, Castillo’s vice president, succeeded Castillo following his impeachment, becoming Peru’s first female president. She was set to serve out the remainder of Castillo’s term until July 2026. However, her tenure was [plagued](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/10/world/americas/peru-president-boluarte-impeached.html) by low approval ratings, increased crime, and several [scandals](https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/10/americas/peru-president-dina-boluarte-removed-intl-hnk). The most prominent of these was “[Rolexgate](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn4jl0xw35xo),” which involved allegations that Boluarte accepted luxury Rolex watches and other expensive jewelry as bribes. Her administration was also characterized by high levels of public insecurity, with several major anti-government protests resulting in the [deaths of dozens](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/peru-government-protests-dozens-killed-political-unrest-pedro-castillo-dina-boluarte/) of demonstrators. Boluarte survived eight impeachment attempts before Congress ultimately [ousted](https://www.cfr.org/articles/president-boluarte-impeached-perus-crisis-runs-deeper) her. #### José Jerí _October 2025–February 2026_ After Boluarte’s impeachment, president of Congress Jerí ascended to the presidency. He was set to lead Peru until July 2026, when a newly elected president would be inaugurated. Yet Jerí quickly became embroiled in a [scandal](https://www.cnn.com/2026/02/17/americas/peru-president-jose-jeri-ousted-intl-latam) stemming from undisclosed, late-night meetings with Chinese businessman Zhihua Yang, who [has](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/23/world/americas/peru-president-chinese-businessmen-meetings.html) more than a dozen companies in Peru. Jerí also faced [accusations](https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/02/02/cinco-allegadas-de-jose-jeri-que-acudieron-a-su-oficina-personal-hasta-casi-la-medianoche-obtuvieron-contratos-estatales/) of awarding state contracts to women following after-hours meetings in the presidential palace. Just four months into Jerí’s term, Congress voted 75–24 to remove him, citing “moral incapacity.” He denied any wrongdoing on both counts. #### José María Balcázar _February 2026–present_ After Jerí was ousted, Congress elected Balcázar, a lawmaker from the left-wing Free Peru Party and a former judge, to serve as interim president until July 28. In his [inauguration speech](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ht359z72pBY), he warned that democracy in Peru was “not working,” but pledged to ensure a peaceful and transparent electoral process, fight crime, and support the economy. Balcázar is no stranger to political controversy, either. He was removed from his former position as a provisional member of Peru’s Supreme Court for serious misconduct and expelled from a regional bar association for alleged [misappropriation of funds](https://larepublica.pe/sociedad/2021/05/07/fiscalia-formalizo-investigacion-preparatoria-contra-exdecano-del-ical-lrnd) during his tenure as its dean. _Surina Venkat contributed to this article._

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of those who have served as [President of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru "President of Peru") ([head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru")) from its establishment to the present. The office was established by the [1822 Constituent Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru_(1822) "Constituent Congress of Peru (1822)"), after the resignation of [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") to his position as Protector of Peru and his subsequent departure from the country.

The first president was [José de la Riva Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_la_Riva_Ag%C3%BCero "José de la Riva Agüero") and the current officeholder is [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar "José María Balcázar"). In the history of the position, there has been several political crises, [caudillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudillo "Caudillo"), barracks revolt, civil wars, death of the incumbent, coups d'état, parliamentary attempts to remove the presidency,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-1) one [self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup "1992 Peruvian self-coup"), and vacancies dictated by the congress. The list is based on the official list of rulers by the Peruvian Congress, as well as the constitutions, laws, and decrees in each case.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-3)

Even though they were not presidents, the list includes the [Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertadores "Libertadores") San Martín and [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar") due to their historical relevance in the independence of Peru and its consolidation. The country's name was changed from "Peruvian Republic" (_República peruana_) to "Republic of Peru" (_República del Perú_) in 1980, after the [1979 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Peru_(1979) "Constitution of Peru (1979)") came into effect.

**Far-right:**

**Right wing:**

*   [Civilista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilista_Party "Civilista Party") (_Partido Civil_, PC)
*   [Constitutional Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Party_(Peru) "Constitutional Party (Peru)")(_Partido Constitucional_)
*   [Reformist Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformist_Democratic_Party "Reformist Democratic Party")(_Partido Democrático Reformista_)
*   [Peruvian Democratic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Democratic_Movement "Peruvian Democratic Movement")(_Movimiento Democrático Peruano_, MDP)
*   [National Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Front_(Peru) "National Democratic Front (Peru)")(_Frente Democrático Nacional_)

**Centre-right:**

*   [Peruvian Aprista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Aprista_Party "Peruvian Aprista Party")(_Partido Aprista Peruano_, APRA)
*   [Peruvians for Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvians_for_Change "Peruvians for Change")(_Peruanos Por el Kambio_, PPK)
*   [Popular Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Action_(Peru) "Popular Action (Peru)")(_Acción Popular_, AP)
*   [We Are Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Peru "We Are Peru")(_Partido Democrático Somos Perú, PDSP_)

**Centrist:**

*   [Possible Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Possible_Peru "Possible Peru")(_Perú Posible_, PP)
*   [Purple Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Party "Purple Party")(_Partido Morado_, PM)

**Centre-left:**

*   [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(Peru) "Democratic Party (Peru)")(_Partido Demócrata_, PD)
*   [Peruvian Nationalist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Nationalist_Party "Peruvian Nationalist Party")(_Partido Nacionalista Peruano_, PNP)

**Far-left:**

This Wikipedia list includes a total of 40 presidents and 53 presidencies from 1821 until 2021.

Andrés de Santa Cruz had been the _de facto_ governor of Peru in the name of Bolivar.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_1,_p._180-21)

Continued to claim power until being betrayed by his own men, who reconciled with Orbegoso on 24 April.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_2,_pp._69%E2%80%9375-32)
10.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-36 "Jump up")**Controlled Lima until 30 December 1835, when Orbegoso's troops entered the city, although infighting continued until 6 January 1836. Was defeated in the [Battle of Socabaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Battle_of_Socabaya&action=edit&redlink=1 "Battle of Socabaya (page does not exist)") on 7 February and executed a few days later, on 18 February.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBasadre2014Volume_2,_pp._92%E2%80%93111-35)
11.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-40 "Jump up")**Orbegoso resigned the Peruvian presidency on 3 August 1836, after promoting the creation of the [Peru–Bolivian Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru%E2%80%93Bolivian_Confederation "Peru–Bolivian Confederation") of [Andrés de Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Santa_Cruz "Andrés de Santa Cruz").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-norp-38) He had already been given the "supreme power" on 8 July 1835, dring the war against Salaverry.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-39)
12.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-43 "Jump up")**Already proclaimed Supreme Protector of [South Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Peru "South Peru") (17 March) and [North Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Peru "North Peru") (6 August).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-41)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-norp-38) Ratified by the [Congress of Tacna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Tacna "Congress of Tacna") on 1 May 1837.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-42)
13.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_ref-45 "Jump up")**Orbegoso declared himself independent on 30 July 1838, but was defeated three weeks later by Gamarra's restoration forces at the [Battle of Portada de Guías](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Portada_de_Gu%C3%ADas "Battle of Portada de Guías"), near Lima. Santa Cruz appointed Riva Agüero as his replacement, at [Tarma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarma "Tarma").
