From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of those who have served as [President of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru "President of Peru") ([head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru")) from its establishment to the present. The office was established by the [1822 Constituent Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru_(1822) "Constituent Congress of Peru (1822)"), after the resignation of [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") to his position as Protector of Peru and his subsequent departure from the country.

The first president was [José de la Riva Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_la_Riva_Ag%C3%BCero "José de la Riva Agüero") and the current officeholder is [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar "José María Balcázar"). In the history of the position, there has been several political crises, [caudillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudillo "Caudillo"), barracks revolt, civil wars, death of the incumbent, coups d'état, parliamentary attempts to remove the presidency,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-1) one [self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup "1992 Peruvian self-coup"), and vacancies dictated by the congress. The list is based on the official list of rulers by the Peruvian Congress, as well as the constitutions, laws, and decrees in each case.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-3)

Even though they were not presidents, the list includes the [Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertadores "Libertadores") San Martín and [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar") due to their historical relevance in the independence of Peru and its consolidation. The country's name was changed from "Peruvian Republic" (_República peruana_) to "Republic of Peru" (_República del Perú_) in 1980, after the [1979 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Peru_(1979) "Constitution of Peru (1979)") came into effect.

**Political parties:**

**Far-right:**

*   [Fujimorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujimorism "Fujimorism")(_Cambio 90_/ _Let's Go Neighbor_)
*   [Revolutionary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Union_(Peru) "Revolutionary Union (Peru)")(_Unión Revolucionaria_, UR)
*   [Odriist National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odriist_National_Union "Odriist National Union")(_Unión Nacional Odriista_, UNO)

**Right wing:**

*   [Civilista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilista_Party "Civilista Party") (_Partido Civil_, PC)
*   [Constitutional Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Party_(Peru) "Constitutional Party (Peru)")(_Partido Constitucional_)
*   [Reformist Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformist_Democratic_Party "Reformist Democratic Party")(_Partido Democrático Reformista_)
*   [Peruvian Democratic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Democratic_Movement "Peruvian Democratic Movement")(_Movimiento Democrático Peruano_, MDP)
*   [National Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Front_(Peru) "National Democratic Front (Peru)")(_Frente Democrático Nacional_)

**Centre-right:**

*   [Peruvian Aprista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Aprista_Party "Peruvian Aprista Party")(_Partido Aprista Peruano_, APRA)
*   [Peruvians for Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvians_for_Change "Peruvians for Change")(_Peruanos Por el Kambio_, PPK)
*   [Popular Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Action_(Peru) "Popular Action (Peru)")(_Acción Popular_, AP)
*   [We Are Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Peru "We Are Peru")(_Partido Democrático Somos Perú, PDSP_)

Title: Why Peru has had 7 presidents in 6 years: Legacy of Fujimori dictatorship’s constitution

URL Source: https://geopoliticaleconomy.com/2022/12/17/peru-7-presidents-6-years-fujimori-constitution/

Published Time: 2022-12-17T22:30:39+00:00

Markdown Content:
In just over six years, Peru has had seven different presidents. The period between July 2016 and December 2022 has been a time of deep political instability.

This chaos is largely due to Peru’s deeply undemocratic constitution, which was inherited from the far-right US-backed dictator Alberto Fujimori, who governed the country with an iron fist from 1990 until 2000, committing [genocide against the Indigenous population](https://twitter.com/BenjaminNorton/status/1551285847596605440) and killing, torturing, and disappearing thousands of dissidents.

[Article 113 of Peru’s constitution](https://www2.congreso.gob.pe/sicr/RelatAgenda/constitucion.nsf/constitucion/1A33E212F19320E50525672900812783) gives the unicameral congress the ability to remove presidents if two-thirds of members vote to declare that they have a “moral incapacity.”

Fujimori wrote this constitution in 1993, after launching a self-coup against Peru’s democratic institutions the year before. Peruvian journalist, scholar, and former lawmaker [Manuel Benza Pflücker explained](http://revista-libertad.com/analisis-politico/la-constitucion-de-la-dictadura-del-93-por-encargo-de-eeuu/) that the Fujimori constitution was largely created by the United States in order to make neoliberal economic policies a mandatory part of the state structure:

> The proximity between the coup d’état and the convocation of a constituent assembly shows us that the main reason for the 1992 coup d’état (Alberto Fujimori’s self-coup) was the drafting of a new constitution according to the ‘Washington Consensus’ (WC), a document that was delivered in New York to Fujimori by authorities of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Department of the Treasury of the United States of America and the World Bank, institutions controlled by said country, days before take an oath to the presidency of Peru. The WC had been prepared a few months before by the aforementioned organizations, under the responsibility of [neoliberal economist] John Williamson and representatives of the establishment.

Although the gap between rich and poor in Peru has grown much wider since the acceleration of neoliberalism in the 1980s, a strong racial element remains quite apparent as well.

According to the 2017 national census, although Peru is only 5.9% white, yet four out of these last seven presidents (57%) are of European descent, making this demographic over-represented in the president’s office by a factorial of nearly 10 times.

Since December 7, 2022, the majority of the Peruvian population seems to have gotten fed up with the perpetual economic and racial disparities, and mass protests have broken out mostly in the southern region of Peru, concentrated in cities such as Arequipa, Cusco, Puno, Ayacucho, and Andahuaylas, in addition to the northern Andean city of Cajamarca, where President Pedro Castillo is from.

At least 25 protesters were killed in the first 10 days of the unelected regime of Dina Boluarte.

The following timeline shows how quickly Peruvian heads of state have changed, and provides a brief summary of why.

![Image 1: Peru Pedro Pablo Kuczynski](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Peru-Pedro-Pablo-Kuczynski.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Pedro Pablo Kuczynski

### President Pedro Pablo Kuczynski Godard (1)

**Term**

July 28, 2016 to March 23, 2018

**Background**

Kuczynski attended elite universities – Oxford University in England and Ivy League Princeton University in New Jersey.

He worked at the World Bank, which has trapped countries across Latin America in debt. He also worked at New York-based investment banks and U.S. mining corporations.

Kuczynski was a U.S. national who renounced his citizenship in November 2015, in order to make himself eligible to become president of Peru.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

Leaked video showed supporters of Kuczynski apparently attempting to bribe members of Congress to cast their votes in Kuczynski’s favor, in the infamous “Mamanivideos” scandal.

After serving 20 months, Kuczynski resigned on March 23, 2018.

![Image 2: Martín Vizcarra Peru](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/martin-vizcarra-Peru.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Martín Vizcarra

### President Martín Vizcarra (2)

**Term**

March 23, 2018 to November 9, 2020

**Background**

Vizcarra was Kuczynski’s protégé, vice president, and close ally. He became wealthy through several family companies and made his name as a conservative governor of Moquegua.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

Allegations of corruption during his term as the governor of Moquegua brought Vizcarra down.

After a congressional debate on November 9, 2020, the congress approved the removal of Vizcarra (in his second impeachment) due to “moral incapacity,” with 105 votes in favor – surpassing the 87 out of 130 vote supermajority threshold (67%) required to remove a political official.

He served as president for two years and eight months, with a temporary disruption in September to October 2019.

![Image 3: Mercedes Aráoz Kuczynski Almagro OAS](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Mercedes-Araoz-Kuczynski-Almagro-OAS.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Mercedes Aráoz (right) with Kuczynski and coup-plotting OAS chief Luis Almagro

### President Mercedes Aráoz (3)

**Term**

September 30 to October 1, 2019

**Background**

Aráoz is a neoliberal economist who received her Master’s and PhD degrees from the University of Miami. She subsequently worked with U.S.-based organizations like the World Bank, the Organization of American States (OAS), and Inter-American Development Bank.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

Vizcarra dissolved the congress on September 30, 2019. In response, the [congress suspended Vizcarra as president](https://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-america-latina-49902304), making his second vice president, Aráoz, temporary president.

With just one day in office, Aráoz never actually came to govern, and resigned the very next day. Vizcarra was quickly returned as president.

![Image 4: Manuel Merino Peru](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Manuel-Merino-Peru.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Manuel Merino

### President Manuel Merino (4)

**Term**

November 10 to 15, 2020

**Background**

Merino is from the city of Tumbes, the most right-wing region of Peru, and is a lifelong conservative.

As president of congress, Merino was criticized regarding how hastily he pushed for impeachment proceedings against Vizcarra, who didn’t have a vice president at the time, which would have made Merino next in line to become president.

Two months later, Merino succeeded in his quest and ousted Vizcarra.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

Merino lasted only five days as president, before resigning due to mass protests against him, which left two young Peruvians dead.

![Image 5: Francisco Sagasti Peru](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Francisco-Sagasti-Peru.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Francisco Sagasti

### President Francisco Sagasti Hochhausler (5)

**Term**

November 17, 2020 to July 28, 2021

**Background**

Sagasti Hochhausler established close connections to the United States while attaining a Master’s degree in industrial engineering at Penn State University and a PhD in operational research and social systems science at the Wharton Business School, at the elite Ivy League University of Pennsylvania.

He went on to work at the World Bank.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

Sagasti was named as interim president to serve until Peru’s next election in July 2021, which was the end of the five-year term begun by Kuczynski back in 2016.

![Image 6: Pedro Castillo Peru president](https://i0.wp.com/geopoliticaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Pedro-Castillo-Peru-president.jpg?resize=880%2C495&ssl=1)

Pedro Castillo

### President Pedro Castillo (6)

**Term**

July 28, 2021 to December 7, 2022

**Background**

Castillo is a farmer and teacher who represents the indigenous Andinos, who have had virtually no power in the government in the modern history of Peru.

After becoming well known for leading a teachers’ strike, Castillo ran for president with the Marxist-Leninist party Peru Libre, and he won the 2021 elections.

**Why was their presidential term so short?**

After stating his intention to dissolve congress – which he was legally entitled to do according to [article 134 of Peru’s constitution](https://www2.congreso.gob.pe/sicr/RelatAgenda/constitucion.nsf/NumArticulos/134?openDocument) – Castillo was impeached, removed by the military, and imprisoned without trial on December 7.

Castillo’s five-year term was cut short to less than 17 months. Mass national protests ensued, demanding his release from prison, fresh elections, and a constituent assembly to write a new constitution.

Castillo supporters have blocked major highways all over Peru, impeding national transportation and bringing the country to a virtual standstill.

Without any due process, the unelected Peruvian government subsequently sentenced Castillo to 18 months of “preventative prison.”

### President Dina Boluarte (7)

**Term**

December 7, 2022 until now

**Background**

The neoliberal-appointed “interim” president, who had previously been expelled from the leftist Peru Libre party, was sworn in by congress in order to serve out the last three-and-a-half years of Castillo’s term.

Mass protests across Peru led Boluarte’s unelected government to suspend civil liberties, declaring a nation-wide “state of emergency.”

Boluarte’s unelected government unleashed large numbers of violent police and deployed soldiers into the streets. They shot protesters with live ammunition, even using helicopters to shoot at demonstrators and drop tear gas bombs on them.

Dozens of protesters were killed and hundreds were wounded in the first week of Boluarte’s rule.

While Peruvian civil society organizations accused Boluarte of “[state terrorism](https://twitter.com/DemusPeru/status/1604176680792494080),” the US government strongly supported her, claiming her unelected government was “[democratic](https://twitter.com/USAmbPeru/status/1602737680374276096).”

Title: List of presidents of Peru

URL Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru

Published Time: 2016-12-04T15:51:57Z

Markdown Content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of those who have served as [President of the Republic of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Peru "President of Peru") ([head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru")) from its establishment to the present. The office was established by the [1822 Constituent Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Congress_of_Peru_(1822) "Constituent Congress of Peru (1822)"), after the resignation of [José de San Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_San_Mart%C3%ADn "José de San Martín") to his position as Protector of Peru and his subsequent departure from the country.

The first president was [José de la Riva Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_la_Riva_Ag%C3%BCero "José de la Riva Agüero") and the current officeholder is [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar "José María Balcázar"). In the history of the position, there has been several political crises, [caudillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudillo "Caudillo"), barracks revolt, civil wars, death of the incumbent, coups d'état, parliamentary attempts to remove the presidency,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-1) one [self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup "1992 Peruvian self-coup"), and vacancies dictated by the congress. The list is based on the official list of rulers by the Peruvian Congress, as well as the constitutions, laws, and decrees in each case.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-FOOTNOTECongress_of_Peru2021a-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_Peru#cite_note-3)

Even though they were not presidents, the list includes the [Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertadores "Libertadores") San Martín and [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar") due to their historical relevance in the independence of Peru and its consolidation. The country's name was changed from "Peruvian Republic" (_República peruana_) to "Republic of Peru" (_República del Perú_) in 1980, after the [1979 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Peru_(1979) "Constitution of Peru (1979)") came into effect.

**Political parties:**

**Far-right:**

*   [Fujimorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujimorism "Fujimorism")(_Cambio 90_/ _Let's Go Neighbor_)
*   [Revolutionary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Union_(Peru) "Revolutionary Union (Peru)")(_Unión Revolucionaria_, UR)
*   [Odriist National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odriist_National_Union "Odriist National Union")(_Unión Nacional Odriista_, UNO)

### Official State Nickname of Hawai'i

Hawaii's state nickname is "The Aloha State" (legislation refers to "the aloha state" as the state's popular name). Hawaii is also called "Paradise of the Pacific." [All State Nicknames](https://statesymbolsusa.org/categories/nickname "Nicknames for 50 states")

"[Aloha Spirit](https://statesymbolsusa.org/symbol-official-item/hawaii/cultural-heritage/aloha-spirit "Hawaii state philosophy")" has been defined by legislature as the working philosophy of native Hawaiians; "Aloha" means mutual regard and affection and extends warmth in caring with no obligation in return. "Aloha" is the essence of relationships in which each person is important to every other person for collective existence.

### Official State Nickname of Hawai'i

Hawaii's state nickname is "The Aloha State" (legislation refers to "the aloha state" as the state's popular name). Hawaii is also called "Paradise of the Pacific." [All State Nicknames](https://statesymbolsusa.org/categories/nickname "Nicknames for 50 states")

"[Aloha Spirit](https://statesymbolsusa.org/symbol-official-item/hawaii/cultural-heritage/aloha-spirit "Hawaii state philosophy")" has been defined by legislature as the working philosophy of native Hawaiians; "Aloha" means mutual regard and affection and extends warmth in caring with no obligation in return. "Aloha" is the essence of relationships in which each person is important to every other person for collective existence.

**Hawaii** ( [_hə-WY-ee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-14)[Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language "Hawaiian language"): _Hawaiʻi_[[həˈvɐjʔi,həˈwɐjʔi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hawaiian "Help:IPA/Hawaiian")) is an island [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of the United States, in the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") about 2,000 miles (3,200 km) southwest of [the U.S. mainland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States"). One of the two non-contiguous U.S. states (along with [Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska "Alaska")), it is the only state not on the North American mainland, the only state that is an [archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago"), the only state south of the [Tropic of Cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_of_Cancer "Tropic of Cancer"), one of only two states, along with [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), with regions that have a [tropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_climate "Tropical climate"), and one of the two U.S. states, along with [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"), that were internationally recognized sovereign countries before becoming U.S. states.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-15)

Hawaii consists of 137 [volcanic islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_island "Volcanic island") that make up almost the entire [Hawaiian archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_archipelago "Hawaiian archipelago") (the exception is [Midway Atoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Atoll "Midway Atoll")). Spanning 1,500 miles (2,400 km), the state is [physiographically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_geography "Physical geography") and [ethnologically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnology "Ethnology") part of the [Polynesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesia "Polynesia") subregion of [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-16) Hawaii's ocean coastline is consequently the [fourth-longest in the U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_coastline "List of U.S. states and territories by coastline"), at about 750 miles (1,210 km).[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-17) The eight main islands, from northwest to southeast, are [Niʻihau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ni%CA%BBihau "Niʻihau"), [Kauaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaua%CA%BBi "Kauaʻi"), [Oʻahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O%CA%BBahu "Oʻahu"), [Molokaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moloka%CA%BBi "Molokaʻi"), [Lānaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C4%81na%CA%BBi "Lānaʻi"), [Kahoʻolawe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaho%CA%BBolawe "Kahoʻolawe"), [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui "Maui"), and [Hawaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawai%CA%BBi_(island) "Hawaiʻi (island)"), after which the state is named; the last is often called the "Big Island" or "Hawaiʻi Island" to avoid confusion with the state or archipelago. The uninhabited [Northwestern Hawaiian Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_Hawaiian_Islands "Northwestern Hawaiian Islands") make up most of the [Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papah%C4%81naumoku%C4%81kea_Marine_National_Monument "Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument"), the [largest protected area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_monuments_of_the_United_States "List of national monuments of the United States") in the U.S. and the [fourth-largest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_protected_areas "List of largest protected areas") in the world.

Of the [50 U.S. states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States "List of states and territories of the United States"), Hawaii is the [eighth-smallest in land area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area") and the [11th-least populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States_by_population "List of states and territories of the United States by population"); but with 1.4 million residents, it ranks [13th in population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States_by_population_density "List of states and territories of the United States by population density"). Two-thirds of Hawaii residents live on Oʻahu, home to the state's capital and largest city, [Honolulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu "Honolulu"). Hawaii is one of the most demographically diverse U.S. states, owing to its location in the central Pacific and over two centuries of migration. As one of nine [majority-minority states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majority_minority_in_the_United_States "Majority minority in the United States"), it has the only Asian American plurality, the largest [Buddhist community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism_in_the_United_States "Buddhism in the United States"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-18) and largest proportion of [multiracial people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_people "Multiracial people") in the U.S.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-19) Consequently, Hawaii is a unique [melting pot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melting_pot "Melting pot") of North American and [East Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Asia "East Asia") cultures, in addition to its [indigenous Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") heritage.

Settled by [Polynesians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesians "Polynesians") sometime between 1000 and 1200 CE, Hawaii was home to numerous independent [chiefdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiefdom "Chiefdom").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-:2-20) In 1778, British explorer [James Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cook "James Cook") was the first known non-Polynesian to arrive at the archipelago; early British influence is reflected in the [state flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Hawaii "Flag of Hawaii"), which bears a [Union Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Jack "Union Jack"). An influx of European and American explorers, traders, and whalers soon arrived, leading to the decimation of the once-isolated indigenous community through the introduction of diseases such as [syphilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syphilis "Syphilis"), [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis"), [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox"), and [measles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles "Measles"); the native Hawaiian population declined from between 300,000 and one million to less than 40,000 by 1890.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-OHA-21)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-23) Hawaii became a unified, internationally recognized [kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_Kingdom "Hawaiian Kingdom") in 1810, remaining independent until American and European businessmen [overthrew the monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overthrow_of_the_Hawaiian_Kingdom "Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom") in 1893; this led to [annexation by the U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newlands_Resolution "Newlands Resolution") in 1898. As a strategically valuable [U.S. territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Hawaii "Territory of Hawaii"), Hawaii was [attacked by Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") on December 7, 1941, which brought it global and historical significance, and contributed to America's entry into World War II. Hawaii is the most recent state to [join the union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_Admission_Act "Hawaii Admission Act"), on August 21, 1959.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-24) In 1993, the U.S. government [formally apologized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apology_Resolution "Apology Resolution") for its role in the overthrow of Hawaii's government, which had spurred the [Hawaiian sovereignty movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_sovereignty_movement "Hawaiian sovereignty movement") and has led to ongoing efforts to obtain redress for the indigenous population.

From the late 19th century until the mid-20th century, Hawaii's economy was dominated by a [plantation economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation_economy "Plantation economy"), it remains a major agricultural exporter due to its fertile soil and uniquely tropical climate in the U.S. Its economy has gradually diversified since the mid-20th century, with tourism and military defense becoming the two largest sectors. The state attracts visitors, surfers, and scientists with its diverse natural scenery, tropical climate, abundant public beaches, oceanic surroundings, active volcanoes, and clear skies. However, since the onset of the 21st century, [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change") has wrought existential threats upon Hawaii and its tourism economy, featuring increasing [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought "Drought") and water shortages, [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise "Sea level rise") and hotel flooding in Downtown Honolulu, and [wildfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildfire "Wildfire") threats. These factors are compounded by an aging and declining population, with an exodus emigrating to the [U.S. mainland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._mainland "U.S. mainland"). Hawaii hosts the [U.S. Pacific Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Pacific_Fleet "U.S. Pacific Fleet"), the world's largest naval command, as well as 75,000 employees of the Defense Department.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-:1-25) Hawaii's isolation results in one of the highest [costs of living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost_of_living "Cost of living") in the U.S. However, Hawaii is the third-wealthiest state,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-:1-25) and residents have the longest life expectancy of any U.S. state, at 80.7 years.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-26)

## Etymology

The State of Hawaii derives its name from the name of its largest island, [Hawaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_(island) "Hawaii (island)"). A common explanation of the name of Hawaiʻi is that it was named for [Hawaiʻiloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiiloa "Hawaiiloa"), a figure from Hawaiian oral tradition. He is said to have discovered the islands when they were first settled.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-27)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-28)

The [Hawaiian language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language "Hawaiian language") word _Hawaiʻi_ is very similar to [Proto-Polynesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Polynesian_language "Proto-Polynesian language")_*Sawaiki_, with the [reconstructed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_reconstruction "Internal reconstruction") meaning 'homeland'.[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-30)[Cognates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognate "Cognate") of _Hawaiʻi_ are found in other Polynesian languages, including [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language "Māori language") (_[Hawaiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiki "Hawaiki")_), [Rarotongan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_Islands_Maori "Cook Islands Maori") (_ʻAvaiki_) and [Samoan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samoan_language "Samoan language") (_[Savaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savai%27i "Savai'i")_). According to linguists Pukui and Elbert,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-31) "elsewhere in Polynesia, _Hawaiʻi_ or a cognate is the name of the underworld or of the ancestral home, but in Hawaii, the name has no meaning".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-32)

### Spelling of state name

In 1978, Hawaiian was added to the Constitution of the State of Hawaii as an official state language alongside English.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-33) The title of the state constitution is _The Constitution of the State of Hawaii_. Article XV, Section 1 of the Constitution uses _The State of Hawaii_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-34)[Diacritics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diacritic "Diacritic") were not used because the document, drafted in 1949,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-35) predates the use of the _[ʻokina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CA%BBokina "ʻokina")_⟨ʻ⟩ and the _[kahakō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macron\_(diacritic) "Macron (diacritic)")_ in modern Hawaiian orthography. The exact spelling of the state's name in the Hawaiian language is _Hawaiʻi_.[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-36)

In the [Hawaii Admission Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_Admission_Act "Hawaii Admission Act") that granted Hawaiian statehood, the federal government used _Hawaii_ as the state name, but most official Hawaiian state government publications, departments, and office titles use _Hawaiʻi_, including the [Governor of Hawaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Hawai%CA%BBi "Governor of Hawaiʻi"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-37) the [Hawaiʻi State Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_State_Legislature "Hawaii State Legislature"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-38) the [Hawaiʻi State Judiciary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_State_Judiciary "Hawaii State Judiciary"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-39) the [University of Hawaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi "University of Hawaiʻi"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-40) the [Hawaiʻi State Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seal_of_Hawaii "Seal of Hawaii"),[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-41) the [Flag of Hawaiʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Hawai%CA%BBi "Flag of Hawaiʻi"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-42) and the Hawaiʻi Board on Geographic Names.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-43) The Hawaiʻi Tourism Authority's official policy is to "recognize the importance of using these markings to preserve the indigenous language and culture of Hawaiʻi and use them in all forms of communications."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii#cite_note-tourism-44)
